title: Headline
subtitle: You see, everybody can be world-famous for 15 minutes.

trails.title: "The Aperitif "
trails.description: The Rockin' Pirate is no stranger to the topic list of social criticism. But be careful, she is not some usual public figure. If you want to have a taste of this rock n' roll cocktail, don't shake the bottle before opening up—the advice is to enjoy it while it is in a relatively stable state.

content.text:
PIRATE INVADED RADIO
     ROCK INTRUDED LIFE

{p}Now, everyone has heard of the renown pirate captain, the one who got away from our "Purge of Radio Programs" Movement. She is the owner of many popular tapes and records, a swaying red ship, and the eagle-like eyes which allows her to spot the police from distance.
{p}One will not deny her charm
if you can set aside your
prejudice against this
rebellious public figure.
You would be touched by
her Pirate Radio and the
ideas she has been fighting
for till this day, if you listen to her "filthy" music and what she has to say.
However, this newspaper feels obliged to state that extreme actions such as hijacking other radio frequencies, taking over public broadcast station, or stealing oil from police vehicles should be condemned.
For some stubborn rebels, punishment is still necessary.

London Review, Opinions, 1966, 09(25B):58{img}

trails.title: Opportunism 101
trails.description: There is no model answer for a Great Thief's test. Notes: "Seize the opportunity" is written in the text book 101, no need to read it out loud.

items.text: The farce in Regent Street seems to finish as the siren alarms. The street returns to its quiet status as usual.
Except for a sneaking figure who tries to escape from the fire engine.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Freeze! Routine check.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Your fire engine driving license, please.
He eventually turns around.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Hello, Mr. Officer.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Again?!

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Within a month, you visited the police station 13 times, stirring the pointers of Big Ben, doodling at 10 Downing Street, dyeing Tower Bridge with waterproof paints ...

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: This time, you threw a messy street party, didn't you?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Ahem! It was not a mess, police officer.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: You are suspected of breaking traffic laws. It's reasonable for us to arrest you right now!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Oh, wait, police officer! Wh-What I did is legitimate.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I've applied for the use of fire engine to the sergeant and got approved.
Diggers shows the note in his hand.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Please feel free to check, Mr. Officer.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Humph! I can't believe the sergeant would approve such a ridiculous application.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: That's what he approved.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: But how are you gonna justify those weird bubbles?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Which one are you referring to?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: The Laser Bubble that reflects people's dreams?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: It caused all the people at the square to fall into a deep sleep for two whole days. They experienced the most unexpected but best holiday ever. Honestly, I really envy them.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Or, you mean the classic work of mine, the Revery Bubble?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: If it's convenient to you, could you please disclose the feedback of other officers? I need some inspiration to revise my formulas.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: What did those officers see when they enjoyed my bubbles, surrendered criminals or a promotion announcement?

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Enough! This time, we will absolutely find out the odd ingredients in the bubbles.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: You can't deceive all of us.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Only if you guys can open the water tank.
Diggers points at the fire engine surrounded by police cars.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: At least up to now, you don't have enough evidence, Mr. Officer.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Fine, I now ask you to cooperate with our investigation as the witness.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Ugh ...

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Alright, I'll stay here till you find new evidence.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Eye on him.

items.speaker: Policeman
items.text: Yes sir.
The police officers start to investigate the fire engine. Diggers suddenly bends down and clutches his belly.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Hiss ... Ahhh ...!

items.speaker: Policeman
items.text: What the hell are you doing? Get up off the floor.
The young and naive police officer rudely pulls Diggers up, but he fails to notice a bubble with a reflective surface forming behind him.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Huffff!

items.speaker: Policeman
items.text: Ugh ...

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Nighty night.
He is sneaking to the end of Regent Street and attentively counting his steps—the steps away from the siren, the steps towards freedom.
But it seems that he totally ignores the approaching engine sound and the anxious warning of a pirate.
Back off!
Get out of my way!
The shiny motorcycle draws a beautiful parabola in the sky and eventually lands precisely in the gap between the flower bed and the wall.
The rock girl on the motorcycle crashes into the liberty-seeking suspect.
Ouch ...

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Hiss ...
At least they have arrived at their common destination, Carnaby Street.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Whoa! Are you a first-time driver?
Ahhh! You ruined my game! Boy!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: It's you ...

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Regulus! That rock pirate fraudster!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: You know me?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Damn it. I knew I had to watch out for you undercover cops lying in ambush around the track!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: What makes you think I'm an undercover cop? This is stigmatization!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Uh, well, you're right. Cops shouldn't be wearing such ragged clothes.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: What? This ... this is a demonstration against the materialistic life, the code of freedom!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Ahem. Though you didn't mistake me with those stupid cops, I still suggest you better distinguish us.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Haha, a humorous suggestion! Ragged lad.
A red globe gently falls down next to Regulus.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: There are some slight scratches on the coat, the transmission system functions well, the braking system is not very well ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Mr. APPLe?! You're back.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: ... Your vehicle looks fine.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Captain, are you alright?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: No, I'm not!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I could have won this, but it all went to pot. The ragged lad ruined my game, my chance to be a podium winner. He ruined a rising racing star!!!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Ahem.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I need to warn you again that any defamation might cause a lawsuit.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Hmph!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: It was your fault! You broke into the track, ragged lad!
The chaos here arouses the attention of another batch of people.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Sir, the lawsuit you were talking about ... Are you referring to those who are approaching?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: What? Bloody hell! They found me!
The police officers are getting closer.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Carnaby Street, call for backup.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: According to the latest update from Sergeant William, his seal has been stolen.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: The suspect, Diggers, is suspected of committing a series of crimes, including illegally using fire engines, forging police ID, attacking police officer ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ugh!

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: We also found someone illegally held an MRR competition on the street, and the suspect is likely Regulus, the rock pirate on the wanted list.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Ugh!

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: You two, freeze! Cooperate with our investigation.

items.speaker: Regulus & Diggers
items.text: Whoa! Run!
Someone escapes, while someone unfortunately gets arrested.
Either of them has to lose the game, sadly.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Is he alright?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Maybe, if all his statements are to be believed.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Do you remember what he said at the end?

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: He told us to read tomorrow's newspaper, the headline.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Is that an obituary or something? Mr. APPLe, I'm going to add a special session for Rock Radio tonight.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: "The Worst Beginning and the Best Ending—To Our Forever Ragged Lad"
TO BE CONTINUED ...
